subject: Vectorstore synchronization & backfill playbook — OpticSearch onboarding
messages:
From: Alex Wu <alex.wu@opticsearch.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben@redwood.com>
Cc: tessa_morgan <tessa@redwood.com>, Priya Sharma <priya@opticsearch.com>
Date: 2026-09-14T16:12:00Z
Subject: OpticSearch — vectorstore sync kickoff and data readiness

Hi Vanessa / Ben —

Thanks for the demo last week. We're ready to start the embedding + rerank onboarding sprint and want to align on the backfill strategy for our historical product docs (approx 1.2M records). A few constraints from our side:

- We need a zero-downtime read path for search during backfill.
- Retention policy: 13 months active, then archive.
- Must preserve original_doc_id mapping and text-level provenance (author/date).

High level ask: can Redwood help run an incremental backfill that keeps our current search live, provides a staged verification bucket, and hands off a final index snapshot for our data team?

I've attached our current table schema and a small sample export. Also looping in Priya (data lead) to confirm export formats.

Next steps we want:
1) Proposed backfill window and expected throughput
2) Vector DB recommendations (we currently run a managed Milvus cluster)
3) Outline of rerank eval plan and acceptance criteria

Appreciate any quick wins we can take in the first week so we can show momentum to our execs.

Alex
Product & Search Lead
OpticSearch

Attachments: optic_schema_sample.csv (sample), historic-export-202608.zip (0.6 GB)

From: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
To: Alex Wu <alex.wu@opticsearch.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben@redwood.com>, tessa_morgan <tessa@redwood.com>, Priya Sharma <priya@opticsearch.com>
Date: 2026-09-14T17:05:00Z
Subject: Re: OpticSearch — vectorstore sync kickoff and data readiness

Hi Alex / Priya —

Thanks for the context and the export. Happy to own the project coordination from Redwood's side. High-level plan below; I attached a working mapping spreadsheet (vector-mapping.xlsx) and a schema diff summary (schema-diff.pdf) to make the first sync concrete.

Week 0 (prep) — 3 business days
- Confirm canonical field mapping (original_doc_id, title, body, metadata). See tab "field-map" in the attached.
- Agree on blackout windows for any heavy writes to your primary DB (we'll do a rolling backfill to avoid lock contention).

Week 1-2 (seed + smoke) — target 50k/day to validate pipelines
- Seed index into a staging vectorstore (isolated namespace).
- Run a 5k-item rerank smoke test against your top queries; compare precision@5 vs baseline.

Week 3-6 (bulk backfill) — parallelized, throttled
- Bulk batches (recommended 20k–50k documents per job depending on vector size).
- Continuous verification job writes a sidecar verification table we can query for sample stories.

Cutover (post-backfill)
- Final sync and snapshot export; enable routing from staging to prod namespace behind a feature flag for a 48h validation window.

Vector DB recommendation: since you're on managed Milvus, we propose two options:
A) Keep Milvus and use Redwood’s staging namespace + prefix-key routing (lowest migration risk).
B) Migrate to Pinecone for smaller vectors / high availability use cases — recommended if you plan multi-regional replicas later.

Rerank eval: we'll provide a template with labeled queries and expected top-5 results. Acceptance criteria we usually use:
- precision@5 >= baseline - 3% (or better)
- no more than 2 regressions in top-10 for a 200-query core set

Questions for you before we finalize schedule:
1) Can Priya share a CSV export of the key fields and an S3 location / access?
2) Any internal restrictions on encryption in transit / at rest beyond SOC2?

I'll put proposed milestone dates into the shared Drive and HubSpot. Can we schedule a 30-min technical kickoff tomorrow?

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference

Attachments: vector-mapping.xlsx, schema-diff.pdf
Related link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-vector-onboard

From: ben_carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Alex Wu <alex.wu@opticsearch.com>
Cc: tessa_morgan <tessa@redwood.com>, Priya Sharma <priya@opticsearch.com>
Date: 2026-09-15T10:34:00Z
Subject: Re: OpticSearch — vectorstore sync kickoff and data readiness

Vanessa / Alex —

A few engineering notes from my side after reviewing the sample export and schema diff. TL;DR: Milvus is fine; main work will be around sharding strategy and KV cache for rerank latency.

Key considerations:
- Vector size & dims: confirm average tokenized vector dims (are you using 1536 or 1024?). This affects memory+shard sizing.
- Backfill pattern: prefer steady streaming of batches (20k max) with stateful retries vs giant one-shot jobs. This keeps CPU/GPU consistent and preserves SLOs.
- Prefix caching: we'll enable prefix KV caching in staging so rerank + contextual prompts hit cached embeddings for frequent ids.
- Consistency: store a version tag with each vector (model-v1, quantized-q4_0) so we can A/B older vs newer vectors during rerank evals.

Operational checklist (we'll coordinate tasks into HubSpot):
- Export format validated: newline-delimited JSON or compressed Parquet preferred.
- Backfill job idempotency: ensure each job writes a manifest on completion (helps resume).
- Monitoring: token cost projection + per-job throughput metrics; set alert at >10% deviation.

On Pinecone vs Milvus: Pinecone gives easier managed replication and namespace isolation; Milvus gives more control over custom index types (IVF-PQ) and is cheaper at scale for heavy vector dims. We can prototype both in Week 1 if you'd like — takes ~1 day to spin up a test namespace + sample ingestion.

I'll attach a small ingestion script stub and job-size recommendations into the Drive.

-ben
Ben Carter
Senior Infra Engineer | Redwood Inference

Thanks team — quick clarifications from our security/compliance side:

- We require KMS-backed encryption for any snapshots that leave our VPC.
- Audit logs for backfill jobs must be retained for 12 months and include job ids / user ids.
- Can Redwood sign a short exception for access to our staging namespace for the duration of the backfill? We'll provide temporary IAM roles.

I've attached our security questionnaire (security-questions.pdf) and added a couple of items we flagged. Let me know if Redwood needs anything additional (SLA/POC).

Priya: can you confirm the S3 bucket role so Vanessa can start the data pull?

Alex

Attachments: security-questions.pdf

Alex / Priya —

Great — summary and next steps below. I've also created the HubSpot playbook card and linked the Drive artifacts (see HubSpot link).

Summary of agreements:
- Backfill will run as rolling staged jobs (20k–40k batches) over 3–4 weeks.
- Staging namespace will be provisioned in your existing Milvus cluster; Redwood will ingest and write verification manifests.
- Encryption: all snapshots exports will be KMS-encrypted per your requirement.
- Audit logs: Redwood will publish job-level logs to the agreed S3 path for 12 months.

Action owners & dates:
- Priya: share S3 read role + example NDJSON export (due: 2026-09-17).
- Vanessa: schedule 30-min tech kickoff and share rerank evaluation template (due: 2026-09-17).
- Ben: spin up staging namespace + ingestion stub, run initial 5k smoke (due: 2026-09-20).
- Alex: provide the 200-query core set / priority endpoints for rerank acceptance (due: 2026-09-20).

Acceptance criteria (final):
- precision@5 within -3% of baseline on core 200 queries
- no P0 regressions in top-10 for the sample set

I'll leave this in Vanessa's inbox and we'll move the HubSpot card to "In Progress" once we have Priya's S3 role. Thanks everyone — excited to get this moving.

-Tessa
Technical Program Manager | Redwood Inference
